national_raw_news.content: India and Switzerland today inked five agreements following bilateral talks between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Swiss President Guy Parmelin in New Delhi. These agreements are on Migration and Mobility Partnership, Exchange of Young Professionals, Promotion and Collaboration on Transportation Technologies, Mobility Systems and Infrastructure in Identified Areas, Letter of Intent between Department of Science and Technology and Swiss National Science Foundation and Implementation Arrangement for cooperation in Innovation, Technology Transfer and Entrepreneurship. In a joint press meet, Prime Minister Modi appreciated Swiss President Guy Parmelin’s commitment to India-Switzerland relations. He said that India implemented the historic Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement with the European Free Trade Association, EFTA, countries last October. Mr Modi noted that the agreement was India’s first Free Trade Agreement with a European economic bloc. He described it as an ambitious framework for investment, innovation, employment and shared prosperity. The Prime Minister highlighted that under the agreement, India aims to attract 100 billion US dollars in investment and create ten lakh direct jobs over the next 15 years. Prime Minister Modi said that India and Switzerland have taken several important decisions to enhance market access for Indian exports in Switzerland and further facilitate investment between the two countries. He said, this will increase exports of Indian agricultural products, pharmaceuticals, textiles and engineering goods to Switzerland. Mr Modi said that at the same time, India will attract new Swiss investments in important sectors, such as biotechnology, life sciences, banking, insurance, food processing and sustainability. Prime Minister said, through these initiatives, the two nations will work together to develop trusted supply chains and reliable solutions for the entire world. He said, both the nations today identified new possibilities for cooperation in military exchanges and defence production. Mr Modi said the they have also agreed to further deepen cooperation in nuclear energy. The Prime Minister said, the friendship between India and Switzerland goes back centuries. He said, in the 19th century, Swami Vivekananda saw a glimpse of the Himalayas in the Swiss Alps. Mahatma Gandhi also spent time in Switzerland and interacted with its people. Mr Modi said, the memories of these historic visits continue to resonate in the friendship even today. President Parmelin arrived in New Delhi this morning on a three-day state visit to India, accompanied by a high-level delegation comprising senior officials and business leaders. He was received by Minister of State for Road Transport and Highways Ajay Tamta at the airport. The visiting dignitary was accorded a ceremonial welcome at the forecourt of Rashtrapati Bhavan. President Droupadi Murmu and Prime Minister Narendra Modi welcomed the Swiss President. He was given a tri-services guard of honour. Talking to reporters after the ceremonial welcome, Mr Parmelin said that the visit is an excellent opportunity to emphasise the importance that both Switzerland and India attach to this relationship. He said, the relationship between the two countries is built on shared democratic values, as well as on trust and mutual respect. Swiss President said that his visit is a stepping stone towards further growth, deepening and strengthening of our close, broad and long-standing partnership. External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar also called on President Parmelin. In a social media post, Dr Jaishankar appreciated President Parmelin’s sentiments towards deepening the India-Switzerland partnership, building on the promise of India – EFTA TEPA. He expressed confidence that Mr Parmelin’s meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi will further engagement across a wide range of domains. The visiting dignitary paid floral tributes to Mahatma Gandhi at Rajghat. President Parmelin will meet President Droupadi Murmu this evening. President Murmu will also host an official banquet in the honour of her Swiss Counterpart.

national_raw_news.title: 1 hour ago | National 108 Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal flags off first international cargo vessel from Assam to Bangla...
national_raw_news.content: In a historic milestone for Assam, Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, Shri Sarbananda Sonowal, today flagged off the first international cargo vessel carrying methanol from Dibrugarh to Bangladesh, marking the revival of the Brahmaputra as a global trade route after nearly 80 years. The initiative opens a direct, greener, and cost-effective trade corridor for the Northeast. A new chapter in India’s inland waterways sector began today as a consignment of methanol set sail from the Bogibeel Terminal in Dibrugarh for Pangaon Port in Dhaka, Bangladesh. Flagging off the maiden international cargo voyage, Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways Sarbananda Sonowal expressed confidence that the terminal would usher in significant economic growth for the region. He announced that the Government will establish a new Skill Development Centre for the shipping sector at Bogibeel terminal with an investment of ₹200 crore. The Centre is expected to train 50,000 youths from Assam and the Northeast over the next ten years, equipping them for employment opportunities in the maritime and shipping industry. Assam Chief Minister Dr. Himanta Biswa Sarma joined the flag-off ceremony virtually. The methanol consignment, produced by Assam Petro-Chemicals Limited will travel through the Brahmaputra, designated as National Waterway-2, and the Indo-Bangladesh Protocol Route. The new waterway link is expected to substantially reduce logistics costs for industries in Assam, ease pressure on road transportation, strengthen economic connectivity with Bangladesh, and generate new employment opportunities across the region.

national_raw_news.title: 1 hour ago | Regional News 50 Centre, West Bengal sign MoU for four new airports to boost air connectivity
national_raw_news.content: Four new airports will be developed in West Bengal within the next two years to boost air connectivity. A Memorandum of Understanding to this effect was signed today between the Centre and the state government at Nabanna in presence of the Civil Aviation Minister K. Ram Mohan Naidu and Chief Minister of West Bengal Suvendu Adhikari. Mr Naidu said the plan includes civil enclaves at Hasimara and Kalaikunda, expansion of Balurghat airport and construction of a new airport in Purulia. He said the 2,700-metre runway at Kalaikunda will be able to handle aircraft such as Boeing 737 and Airbus A320. Plans are also underway for a new terminal at Bagdogra, more international flights from Kolkata and direct connectivity with Europe. Mr Naidu said the number of airports in the country has increased from 74 in 2014 to 166 now. Under the revised UDAN scheme, another 100 airports are planned over the next ten years, with four in West Bengal being given priority. Chief Minister Adhikari urged the Centre to introduce direct flights from Kolkata to European cities and expand connectivity from Andal to major destinations. He also sought direct flights to Ayodhya, Tirupati and Amritsar. Mr Adhikari said work has begun on a proposal for a second international airport for Kolkata at Kalyani, on around 2,000 acres of land. He also sought approval for a flying training institute at Behala. The new airports, he said, would boost agriculture, tourism, industry, investment, employment and regional connectivity.

national_raw_news.title: India signs off with 85 medals after Gold rush in cricket, hockey & Kabaddi at Asian Games 15 hours ago 361
national_raw_news.content: India concluded its campaign at the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya with 85 medals, including 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze, finishing fourth in the overall standings. India’s 2026 Asian Games campaign produced a series of landmark achievements across disciplines. The defining feature of India’s campaign was its clean sweep of gold medals in men’s and women’s cricket, kabaddi and hockey. The Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games concluded yesterday, bringing more than two weeks of exciting sporting action to an end. In cricket, India retained both titles. The women’s team defeated Sri Lanka by 147 runs in the final, while the men’s team overcame Pakistan by 19 runs to complete the golden double. Kabaddi also produced a clean sweep. The women’s team defeated Iran 37-34 to successfully defend its title, while the men came from behind to beat Iran 40-34. Hockey also completed the sweep. The Indian women ended a 44-year wait for an Asian Games medal by defeating China 1-0, with Lalremsiami scoring the decisive goal in the 10th minute. It was India’s first women’s hockey gold at the Asian Games since 1982. The men’s team defeated Malaysia 5-1 to retain its title and claim India’s fifth men’s hockey gold, following triumphs in 1966, 1998, 2014 and 2022. It was also the first time India’s men’s and women’s hockey teams won gold at the same Asian Games. Both teams secured qualification for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics. Archery was one of India’s most successful disciplines, producing nine medals – five gold, two silver and two bronze. Boxing produced India’s best Asian Games campaign in terms of gold medals, with three gold and three bronze medals. Indian wrestlers won six medals – two gold, two silver and two bronze, making it the country’s best Asian Games wrestling tally since Jakarta 1962.
